 No. 1 / State.

Mr. Upendra Yadav - Advocate for respondent No. 2.
 Order

Present petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing of FIR at Crime No.201/2021 registered at Police Station - Thatipur, District - Gwalior (M.P.) for offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC as well as its consequential proceedings in respect to present petitioner.

As per prosecution story, on 26.3.2021, respondent No. 2 / complainant lodged a written complaint at the police station to the effect that present petitioner / accused took loan of Rs.27,00,000/- from him for establishing a beauty parlor and petrol pump, however, he did not return the money even after four years.
Upon this, FIR bearing Crime No. 201/2021 was registered against the present petitioner for offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 2 MCRC-47791-2023
Learned counsels for the petitioners submitted that this false FIR has been lodged against the petitioner.
There is no material available on record to support the allegations made by the complainant.

It is further argued that even if the entire prosecution story is accepted, the case appears to be of civil nature and complainant is trying to give it the colour of criminal case and false FIR has been lodged with malafide intention.

Therefore, FIR registered at Crime No.201/2021 registered against the present Jitendra Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179603119/
1 petitioner for offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC as well as its consequential proceedings pending against the petitioner be quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned State counsel a well as learned Senior Counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the petition and argued that there is specific allegation against the petitioner in the FIR of cheating and criminal breach of trust.
Further submission is that while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the defence of the accused persons cannot be looked into.
Hence, FIR registered against the petitioner and its consequential proceedings cannot be quashed and prayed to dismiss this petition.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.

The main argument of learned counsel for the petitioner is that respondent No. 2 / complainant has filed the FIR with malafide intention because nature of dispute appears to be of civil nature and complainant is trying to give it colour of criminal case.

In support of his contention, he relied upon the caw law of V.Y. Jose vs. State of Gujarat; (2009) 3 SCC 78 .
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22040 3 MCRC-47791-2023

entities.text: V.Y. Jose vs. State of Gujarat; (2009) 3 SCC 78
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the facts and circumstances of that case are different from the present case and, therefore, it cannot help the petitioner.
Even otherwise, in the aforesaid case, Hon'ble Supreme Court has also held that only because civil law can be taken recourse would not necessarily mean that criminal proceedings should be barred.
However, there exists a distinction between pure contractual dispute of a civil nature and an offence of cheating.

In the case of Rishipal Singh Vs State of U.P. And Another A.I.R. 2014 S.C.2567, the Supreme Court has laid down that while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. before quashing of complaint at the initial stage, the tests to be applied by the Court is as to whether the uncontroverted allegations as made in the complaint prima facie establish the offence.

entities.text: Rishipal Singh Vs State of U.P. And Another A.I.R. 2014 S.C.2567
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above case laws, while examining this case, from the perusal of FIR and other evidence available in the case diary, prima facie ingredients of offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC are found to be available.

Therefore, this Court does not find it fit to quash the FIR at Crime No.201/2021 registered at Police Station - Thatipur, District - Gwalior (M.P.) for offence under Sections 420 and 406 of IPC against the petitioner.
Accordingly, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE AKS Jitendra Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179603119/
